01.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
01.event: The two sages were about to permit a nursing mother whose child was weaned or given to a wet nurse to remarry immediately, following a baraita.
01.turn: An old woman told them Rav Nahman had forbidden exactly this in her own case, and Rav Pappi reminded them of Rabbi Meir's decree and Shmuel's ruling that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees.
01.outcome: They admitted they had forgotten the principle, and the halakha was fixed: if the child died she may remarry, if weaned she may not.
01.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua planned to rule that a nursing mother who had given her child to a wet nurse could remarry at once. An old woman told them that when this happened to her, Rav Nahman forbade it. Rav Pappi then cited a baraita and Shmuel's principle that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's protective decrees, and the two sages admitted they had forgotten it.

02.actor: A depositor and the family of Rabbi Meyasha
02.event: A man deposited seven pearls wrapped in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without telling his household whose they were.
02.turn: The dispute came before Rabbi Ami, who knew Rabbi Meyasha was not wealthy enough to own such pearls.
02.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded the pearls to the claimant, who had also given an identifying mark.
02.summary: A man left seven pearls tied in a sheet at the house of Rabbi Meyasha, grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. Rabbi Meyasha died without saying whose they were, and the case came before Rabbi Ami. He ruled for the depositor, because he knew Rabbi Meyasha could not have afforded such gems and because the depositor described a distinguishing mark.

03.actor: The daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon
03.event: The Sages allotted her four hundred gold coins a day for perfumes from her late husband's estate.
03.turn: Instead of thanking them simply, she told them they should allot as much for their own daughters, a remark that could be heard as a blessing or as a jab.
03.summary: When the Sages set the perfume allowance for Nakdimon ben Guryon's widowed daughter at four hundred gold coins for that one day, she told them: may you pledge the same for your own daughters. The Sages answered after her, 'Amen.'

04.actor: A man testifying before Rabbi Ami
04.event: A man told Rabbi Ami that someone held presumptive status as a priest because he read first from the Torah.
04.turn: Rabbi Ami questioned whether he read first as a priest or as a prominent scholar, and the witness answered that a Levite read after him.
04.outcome: Rabbi Ami elevated the man to the priesthood on the witness's word.
04.summary: A man came to Rabbi Ami and testified that another man was presumed to be a priest because he had been called first to the Torah. Rabbi Ami asked whether that might have been out of honor for a great scholar; the witness replied that a Levite was called right after him, which only happens after a priest. On that basis Rabbi Ami recognized him as a priest.

06.actor: A man's daughter and his heirs
06.event: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter, but the orphans divided the estate without giving her one.
06.turn: Rav Yosef thought each heir could deflect her, as in the mishna, but Abaye objected that here the tree was owed by all of them together.
06.outcome: Abaye ruled they must give her a palm tree and redivide the estate from the start.
06.summary: A man left instructions that his daughter receive a palm tree, but his heirs split the property and left her with none. Rav Yosef first compared it to a case where each party can claim the obligation lies with someone else. Abaye disagreed, saying the tree was the shared obligation of all the heirs, and ruled that they must give her a tree and divide the estate again.

07.actor: Two men whose lineage was mocked
07.event: People called one man 'son of the Aramean woman' and another 'son of the Aramean man,' casting doubt on a parent's conversion.
07.turn: Rav Asi and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi pointed out that the parent's later ritual immersions for purity counted as immersion for conversion.
07.summary: One man was taunted as the son of an Aramean woman, implying his mother's conversion was invalid; Rav Asi answered that she had surely immersed for her menstrual purity. Another was taunted as the son of an Aramean man, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi answered that the father had surely immersed after a seminal emission. Both immersions were taken as sufficient for conversion.
07.missing: An explicit statement of how the cases ended (that the men were declared of unflawed lineage) is implied but not stated.

08.event: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer, and then Rabbi Yehoshua, whether to honor his father or mother first when both ask for water.
08.turn: When he pressed Rabbi Yehoshua about a divorced mother, Rabbi Yehoshua saw from his tearful eyes that he was a widow's son with no father, so the question was idle.
08.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua answered him sarcastically: pour water in a basin and cluck at them like chickens.
08.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer which parent to serve first if both asked for water; he was told the father, since the mother too must honor the father. Rabbi Yehoshua gave the same answer. When the young man asked what if the mother is divorced, Rabbi Yehoshua said his tear-filled eyes showed he was a widow's son and had no father, and mockingly told him to pour water in a basin and call them like chickens.

10.event: When a man was presumed a priest because he read first from the Torah, Reish Lakish asked whether he had received teruma, and Rabbi Elazar objected; later the same case came before Rabbi Yohanan.
10.turn: Rabbi Yohanan made exactly Rabbi Elazar's objection, revealing that Rabbi Elazar had been quoting him without attribution.
10.outcome: Reish Lakish glared at Rabbi Elazar and rebuked him for repeating bar Nappaha's words without saying whose they were.
10.summary: Reish Lakish once refused to accept a man as a priest on the basis of reading first from the Torah, asking whether he had received teruma at the threshing floor; Rabbi Elazar retorted that priesthood cannot depend on a threshing floor. Later, sitting before Rabbi Yohanan, the same kind of case came up and Rabbi Yohanan gave Rabbi Elazar's very answer. Reish Lakish looked sharply at Rabbi Elazar and complained that he had heard this from Rabbi Yohanan and not cited him.

11.event: A man deposited sesame with a friend and later asked for it back.
11.turn: The friend claimed the owner had already taken it; the owner described the amount and barrel, and the friend said the sesame there was different.
11.summary: A man left sesame with a friend and later asked for it. The friend said he had already taken it back. The owner pointed to a barrel holding exactly the amount he had deposited, but the friend insisted that sesame was someone else's.
11.missing: The ruling that resolved the dispute.

12.actor: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ami's slave and a gentile woman
12.event: Rabbi Hiyya bar Ami's slave had a gentile woman immerse so that he could have relations with her.
12.turn: Rav Yosef said he could declare both her and her daughter fit to marry into Israel.
12.summary: A slave of Rabbi Hiyya bar Ami had a gentile woman immerse for the sake of relations with him. Rav Yosef declared that he could rule both her and her daughter fit to marry Jews.
12.missing: Whether he actually ruled so and the reasoning, which follows in later segments.

13.event: Bonyos sent Rabbi an ancient se'a measure from Na'usa.
13.outcome: Rabbi measured it and found it held 217 eggs.
13.summary: Rav Dimi reported that a man named Bonyos sent Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi a se'a measure from Na'usa. Rabbi measured it and found that it held 217 eggs.

14.event: Rabbi Banai held movable property belonging to orphans.
14.turn: The orphan daughters came before Shmuel seeking support.
14.outcome: Shmuel told Rabbi Banai to go and sustain them from it.
14.summary: Rabbi Banai, brother of Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba, was holding movable property left by a dead man for his children. The orphan daughters brought the matter to Shmuel, who told Rabbi Banai to provide for them from that property.

15.event: A gentile superintendent living near Rabbi Zeira refused to rent his domain to the neighbors for an eiruv.
15.turn: The neighbors asked Rabbi Zeira whether they could rent it from his wife instead.
15.outcome: Rabbi Zeira ruled, citing Rabbi Hanina, that a man's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge.
15.summary: A gentile official lived in Rabbi Zeira's neighborhood and would not rent his domain to the Jewish neighbors so they could carry on Shabbat. They asked Rabbi Zeira whether renting from his wife would work. He answered with a teaching of Rabbi Hanina, via Reish Lakish, that a wife may make an eiruv without her husband knowing, so they could.

16.actor: A man who sold his mother's ketubah rights
16.event: A man sold his future rights to his mother's ketubah, stipulating he would not reimburse the buyer if his mother objected.
16.turn: His mother died without objecting, and he himself contested the sale, claiming to stand in her place.
16.outcome: Rava rejected the claim: he had at least guaranteed the sale against his own objections.
16.summary: A man sold the rights to his mother's ketubah for a sum, telling the buyer he would not refund him if his mother objected. His mother died without objecting, and then he challenged the sale himself. Rami bar Hama thought he could object in his mother's place, but Rava said that even if he had not guaranteed against her objection, he had certainly guaranteed against his own.

17.event: A bill of divorce was found in the flax house in Pumbedita.
17.outcome: Rabba ruled on it in accordance with his own teaching.
17.summary: A bill of divorce turned up in the flax house in Pumbedita, and Rabba issued a practical ruling on it according to his own halakhic view. Traditions differ on the details of where it was found and the circumstances.
17.missing: What exactly Rabba ruled (whether the get was returned) is not stated in the passage itself.

18.event: Ben Azzai taught that one who does not procreate is like one who sheds blood, yet he himself never married.
18.turn: His colleagues confronted him: he expounds well but does not practice what he preaches.
18.outcome: Ben Azzai replied that his soul yearned for Torah and the world could be sustained by others.
18.summary: After Ben Azzai taught how grave it is not to have children, the sages pointed out that he preached well but did not live by it, since he had never married. Ben Azzai answered that his soul longed for Torah, and that the world could be populated through others.

19.event: A large unenclosed yard in Pum Nahara opened on one side to the town and on the other to a vineyard path ending at a riverbank, and the sages sought a way to permit carrying in it.
19.turn: Abaye rejected a partition on the riverbank and a doorframe the camels would knock down, then proposed a side post at the vineyard path, which Rava rejected as misleading.
19.outcome: Rava proposed instead a side post at the yard's opening to the town.
19.summary: In Pum Nahara there was a yard where carrying on Shabbat was a problem. Abaye considered and rejected a partition on the riverbank and a doorframe that passing camels would knock over, then suggested a side post at the vineyard path. Rava objected that people would wrongly think a side post works for any vineyard path, and suggested placing it at the opening to the town instead.
19.missing: Whether either solution was actually implemented.

20.missing: The incident referred to (at the wagons of Tzippori) is only located, not narrated, in the shown text.
